mechanism_narrative: A 2% quarterly increase in Real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strengthening economic growth, leading to increased consumer spending and, subsequently, higher S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 55% of instances when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2% QoQ over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) falls below 3.5% and Payroll Employment (PAYEMS) growth exceeds 200,000, the tightening labor market predicts increased wage pressures, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this interaction remains below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 5% month-over-month increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) indicates a surge in housing demand, forecasting increased S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to the ripple effect in related industries.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in > 50% of instances when HOUST growth exceeds 5% MoM over the next 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial Production (INDPRO) growth above 2% month-over-month signals increased economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as supply chains respond to demand.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are negative in > 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 2% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: The difference between FEDFUNDS and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) inflation rate (FEDFUNDS - CPIAUCSL) being positive indicates a real interest rate environment, which should lead to decreased S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this spread remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail Sales (RSAFS) growth below -1% month-over-month indicates weakening consumer demand, forecasting decreased S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as retailers and dependent industries adjust.
failure_condition: 20-day forward SPX returns are positive in > 60% of periods when RSAFS growth is below -1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Unemployment Rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over two months signals labor market weakening, leading to increased S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates monetary easing.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during easing periods.
